abstract.p: In Japanese, the form of utterances often reflect speaker-specific character traits, such as gender and personality, through the choise of linguistic elements including personal pronouns and sentence-final particles. However, such elements are not always available in English and a character's traits are often not directly expressed in English utterances, which can lead to character-inconsistent translations of English novels into Japanese. To address this, we propose a character-aware translation framework that incorporates speaker embeddings. We first train a speaker embedding model by masking the expressions in Japanese utterances that manifest the speaker's traits and learning to predict them. The resulting embeddings are then injected into a machine translation model. Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms conventional fine-tuning in preserving speaker-specific character traits in translations.
